title: Supreme Court dismisses petitions vs Rodrigo Duterte’s ICC arrest
summary: 'The Philippine courts cannot enforce the writ since he is already in the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, the Netherlands,' the High Court says

blocks.text: HIGHEST COURT. File photo of the Supreme Court of the Philippines.
'The Philippine courts cannot enforce the writ since he is already in the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, the Netherlands,' the High Court says
MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court (SC), via a majority, dismissed the consolidated petitions questioning the arrest of former president Rodrigo Duterte in March 2025.
This comes days before Duterte’s International Criminal Court (ICC) trial scheduled on November 30.
In a decision penned by Associate Justice Japar Dimaampao released on Tuesday, November 24, the SC said the habeas corpus petitions were already moot or invalid.
“The Philippine courts cannot enforce the writ since he is already in the custody of the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, the Netherlands,” the High Court said.
Nine justices voted to deny the petitions, four dissented, while Associate Justice Samuel Gaerlan was on official business.

The High Court explained that a writ of habeas corpus — an extraordinary legal remedy used against illegal detention — is enforceable only within the Philippines. Duterte has been detained in The Hague since March 2025.

“This reflects the principle that a court cannot exercise authority outside its territory over persons or property located in another State,” the SC said. “Since Duterte is now under ICC custody in The Hague, Philippine courts cannot enforce a writ affecting his detention or release.”
The High Court noted that Duterte “is already participating in ICC proceedings and has pursued remedies available under its rules.”

“His children were also aware of the basis of his detention and were actively challenging it before the ICC. Because 𝘩𝘢𝘣𝘦𝘢𝘴 𝘤𝘰𝘳𝘱𝘶𝘴 examines whether detention prior to transfer to a court is legal, issuing the writ would serve no practical purpose here,” the SC said in its ruling.
Duterte was arrested by local authorities in March 2025 over an ICC warrant. He is facing three counts of crimes against humanity case for murder and attempted murder.
This case stemmed from the killings in his war on drugs and Davao Death Squad.
However, the SC explained that the dismissal of the petition did not mean that Duterte’s arrest and transfer were necessarily legal or that his rights were not violated.
The High Court said the decision only addressed whether habeas corpus is the proper remedy under the current circumstances.

“The SC explained that any purported violation of Duterte’s rights, including claims for compensation or liability, must be pursued through the appropriate legal proceedings rather than through a petition for habeas corpus,” said the ruling. — Rappler.com
